claim_text: Hackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One platform, according to unnamed sources and a US official
summary: Reuters, citing three people familiar with the matter, reports that hackers breached Cloud One, the US Air Force's main cloud platform. NBC News says a US official confirmed it, and Federal News Network's own source confirmed details.
detail: All three outlets rely on people who spoke without being named. None of them says who the hackers were or what they took. The Air Force has not confirmed or denied a breach on the record.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters: hackers "have breached" the platform, "three people familiar with the matter told Reuters". NBC News: "A U.S. official confirms" it "was breached by hackers." Federal News Network: its source "confirmed some details".
notes: Kept at Reported: every outlet rests on unnamed sources, and there is no on-the-record statement.

claim_text: The intrusion was found during work on the platform; the outlets give different times
summary: Reuters reports the intrusion was discovered "within the past month or so" during work to upgrade Cloud One. Federal News Network's source says it was discovered "earlier this year" while a vulnerability was being patched.
detail: How long the intruders were inside is not known.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters: "discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system". Federal News Network: "discovered the breach earlier this year while patching a vulnerability".

claim_text: One source says the intruders used a software flaw to reach the platform's control plane
summary: One of Reuters' sources says the intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane, which that person likened to a universal remote. Reuters says it is unclear whether the hackers used that access.
detail: Reuters could not identify the vulnerability.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters (via Defense News): "One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane" and "it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case."

claim_text: It is not known whether any data was stolen
summary: Reuters says it could not establish who the hackers were, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data was stolen. The Air Force declined to tell Federal News Network what the intruders could reach.
detail: Reuters says the breach could put sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data at risk; that is a possibility, not a finding.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters: it "could not establish ... the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen." Federal News Network: the Air Force "declined to answer what information the intruders were able to access".

claim_text: Finding the intrusion disrupted parts of Cloud One
summary: Reuters' sources say moving back-office applications to Cloud One is paused, updates to applications on it were blocked and some users lost administrator rights. Federal News Network's source says the clean-up disrupted some functions.
detail: Neither outlet says the platform as a whole went down, or when the disruption will end.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters: migration "paused", updates "were blocked", some users "had their administrator rights revoked." Federal News Network: remediation "disrupted some Cloud One functions, including those requiring administrative access".

claim_text: The Air Force will not comment on the security of specific systems
summary: Asked about the breach, the Air Force said it does not comment on the security, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems, and that it continuously takes prudent measures to protect its information and systems.
detail: It declined to tell Federal News Network what was accessed or whether personnel or operations were affected, and declined to tell NBC News how serious it was or who was responsible.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both outlets quote the Air Force. Reuters: it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems." Federal News Network: "We continuously take prudent measures".

claim_text: Cyber Command was called in to assess the damage, one source says
summary: One of Reuters' sources says investigators called in US Cyber Command, the military's cyber force, to assess the damage. Cyber Command did not respond to Reuters.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters (via Defense News): "Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the U.S. military's cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said."

claim_text: Nobody has said who was behind it
summary: Neither Reuters nor Federal News Network could say who the hackers were, and the Air Force has not said.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters (via Defense News): "Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers". Federal News Network: "It's unclear how long the hack lasted, who was responsible or how they entered the system."

claim_text: Cloud One is the Air Force's main cloud platform, launched in 2017
summary: Cloud One was launched in 2017 to give the Air Force one place to run applications on Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle clouds. It hosts personnel, pay, logistics and maintenance systems, and is open across the Defense Department.
detail: Reuters names two systems that run on it: Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collects air defence radar data, and a system that tracks munitions at more than 200 Air Force locations.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reuters: "Initiated in 2017", combining "four operators". Federal News Network: "The Cloud One program launched in 2017" and hosts IT "for military personnel actions and payroll, logistics and maintenance".

claim_text: The report comes amid other recent hacks of US government systems; no source links them
summary: Reuters notes the US government is dealing with at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI and one at the Treasury. Neither Reuters nor Federal News Network says they are connected to Cloud One.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters (via Defense News): "The U.S. government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents". Neither article links them to this breach.

claim_text: Online discussion asks whether AI-powered attackers were behind it
summary: In the Hacker News discussion of the story, several separate commenters ask whether automated or AI-driven attacks were behind it. No source says how the intruders worked beyond one source's account of a software flaw.
detail: This thread is where the question is raised, not evidence of anything.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: The Hacker News thread is where the question is raised; Reuters mentions wider worry about AI-powered intrusions but does not say AI was used here.
